entries: **Nothing changes on screen in this release — it is housekeeping on the menu bar code.** `menubar.py` had reached 2485 lines, creeping past 2000 for the third time after being split apart twice. The icon and alert helpers moved into a new `menubar_chrome.py`, and the state constructors joined `menubar_state.py`, taking the file down to 2230. Only module-level functions moved: PyObjC binds `AppDelegate` methods by selector name, so relocating one would silently stop the matching control from working. `_popover_size` was split rather than moved, because it ends in `NSMakeSize` and `menubar_state.py` has to stay importable without the ObjC runtime for its projections to be unit-testable — the arithmetic moved as `popover_dimensions()` and a three-line shell stayed behind.

**The growth policy behind that cleanup is now enforced by CI rather than by discipline.** `scripts/check_file_size.py` fails the build when a guarded file passes its ceiling. The rule had been written in CLAUDE.md all along; nothing checked it, and the file grew back twice. Lower a ceiling when a cut lands, never raise it to go green.

**CLAUDE.md's module map lists only modules with a gotcha.** Half its rows restated what opening the file would tell you, and three separate rows repeated the same stdlib-only constraint. It went from 24 rows to 12.

title.zh-TW: 看不見的整理：選單列程式分家，尺寸規則自動把關
title.en: Invisible housekeeping: menu bar code gets divided up and size limits get enforced

body.zh-TW: 這版選單列畫面不變，整理藏在牆裡。`menubar.py` 已膨脹到 2,485 行，第三次超過 2,000 行。圖示與警示的輔助程式搬到 `menubar_chrome.py`，狀態建立程式移至 `menubar_state.py`，主檔降至 2,230 行。只移動檔案直屬函式。PyObjC（讓 Python 接上 macOS Objective-C 的橋樑）靠 `AppDelegate` 的方法名稱連接控制項，搬動它會令對應控制項失靈；`_popover_size` 則拆成計算函式，留三行外殼，讓無 ObjC 執行環境的單元測試仍能跑。接著，CI（自動檢查流程）開始替檔案尺寸守門，超限就讓建置失敗；切割檔案時降上限，別為通過檢查抬高它。CLAUDE.md 的模組地圖從 24 列縮到 12 列，只留會踩雷的說明。像整理屋內管線，表面不變，日後維修不必再越鑿越大。
body.en: Nothing new appears in the menu bar in this release; the work is behind the wall. `menubar.py` had grown to 2,485 lines and crossed 2,000 for the third time. Icon and alert helpers now live in `menubar_chrome.py`, while state constructors moved to `menubar_state.py`, bringing the original file down to 2,230 lines. Only file-level functions moved: PyObjC, the bridge between Python and macOS Objective-C, connects controls through `AppDelegate` method names, so moving one would silently break its control. `_popover_size` was split into a calculation function with a three-line shell left behind, keeping `menubar_state.py` testable without the ObjC runtime. CI, the automatic check run on changes, now fails a build when a guarded file exceeds its limit; after a cut, lower the limit rather than raising it to pass. CLAUDE.md's module map also shrank from 24 rows to 12, keeping only warnings that are not obvious from opening each module. It is like reorganizing plumbing: no new fixture appears, but later repairs need not keep breaking through a larger wall.

Only module-level functions moved: PyObjC binds `AppDelegate` methods by selector name, so relocating one would silently stop the matching control from working. `_popover_size` was split rather than moved, because it ends in `NSMakeSize` and `menubar_state.py` has to stay importable without the ObjC runtime for its projections to be unit-testable — the arithmetic moved as `popover_dimensions()` and a three-line shell stayed behind.
**The growth policy behind that cleanup is now enforced by CI rather than by discipline.** `scripts/check_file_size.py` fails the build when a guarded file passes its ceiling. The rule had been written in CLAUDE.md all along; nothing checked it, and the file grew back twice. Lower a ceiling when a cut lands, never raise it to go green.
**CLAUDE.md's module map lists only modules with a gotcha.** Half its rows restated what opening the file would tell you, and three separate rows repeated the same stdlib-only constraint. It went from 24 rows to 12.

entries: **The panel can now be placed anywhere on screen**: it was an `NSPopover`, which AppKit anchors to the status item and dismisses the moment focus moves elsewhere, so where it sat was never yours to choose. It is now a borderless floating panel: drag it from any empty spot, and it reopens where you left it. It stays put when another app takes focus — a second click on the menu bar icon, or Escape, closes it. Rounded corners and the drop shadow came free with the popover and are now drawn by the window itself. Dragging travels over the existing JS bridge: an injected script reports a mousedown that landed outside any interactive or scrollable element, and the window hands the gesture to `performWindowDragWithEvent:` so the system drives it. Resizing pins the top-left corner, because a window's origin is its bottom-left and the panel would otherwise appear to jump every time its height tracked a fresh content measurement.

**The AI Talent Market panel no longer collapses into a squashed strip**: the panel intermittently opened at roughly the height of its own header, cutting off the team list. The dynamic content-height probe releases the layout's height constraints before measuring, and this panel builds its list as an absolutely positioned layer inside a `flex: 1` body — with the constraints released, that body collapsed to zero and the probe reported little more than the header, which the clamp then rounded up to the minimum panel height. Whether it happened came down to measurement timing, hence the intermittency. Panels now carry a switch for the probe, and this one — a fixed-height design that scrolls internally and never needed measuring — opts out.

**Dismissing the switch-panel menu no longer closes the panel**: opening "Switch Panel" and then clicking the panel itself, pressing Escape, or clicking away closed the whole panel. A transient popover was already gone by the time the menu took focus, so closing it was merely cleanup; the floating panel survives the menu, which turned the same cleanup into a mistouch that threw the panel away.

title.zh-TW: 面板能隨你擺放，切換視窗也不會消失
title.en: Put the panel where you want, and keep it there

body.zh-TW: 想把用量面板挪到螢幕邊角，現在直接拖曳空白處就行。它不再只能黏在選單列圖示旁、別的 app 取得焦點就收起，而是無邊框的浮動面板：放到哪裡，下次就從哪裡打開，圓角和陰影也照留著。檢查其他 app 時它仍待在原處；再按一次選單列圖示或按 Escape 才會關。拖曳不會搶走按鈕與捲動區的操作，內容高度變動時也固定左上角，因此不會像量尺從底端拉長般跳來跳去。
body.en: Want the usage panel in a screen corner? Drag any empty spot on it. It is no longer a popover stuck to the menu-bar icon that vanishes when another app gets focus; it is a borderless floating panel that reopens where you left it, with its rounded corners and shadow intact. It stays put while you check another app, and closes only when you click the menu-bar icon again or press Escape. Dragging leaves buttons and scrollable areas alone, while resizing holds the top-left corner still so the panel does not jump like a ruler stretching from its bottom edge.

title.zh-TW: AI 人才市集面板不再縮成一條
title.en: The AI Talent Market panel no longer squashes itself flat

body.zh-TW: AI 人才市集面板有時一打開只剩標題那一條，隊伍清單像被折進抽屜底部；現在不會了。問題不在資料消失，而是它量高度時暫時放開限制，內部採固定高度、自己捲動的清單剛好被量成零高；又因量測時間不同，才會時好時壞。新版讓各面板決定是否參加這個自動量測。人才市集本來就該固定高度、在裡面捲動，現在跳過自動量測，打開就能看到完整隊伍清單。
body.en: The AI Talent Market panel sometimes opened as little more than its header, as if the team list had been folded into the bottom of a drawer. That list was not gone: while the app measured content height, it temporarily released layout constraints, and this fixed-height, internally scrolling list could collapse to zero. Timing made the failure intermittent. Panels can now opt out of that automatic measurement. AI Talent Market was always meant to keep a fixed height and scroll inside it, so it skips the measurement and opens with the full list visible.

title.zh-TW: 切換面板選單收起時，不再連面板一起關
title.en: Closing the Switch Panel menu no longer closes the panel too

body.zh-TW: 點開「切換面板」選單後，想回去看面板卻把整張面板關掉的烏龍沒了。以前選單打開時，原本的彈出式選單已經消失；清理它的動作卻誤把浮動面板當成也該收掉的東西。因此你按 Escape、點面板或點到別處，選單消失的同時面板也消失。現在清理只會關選單，浮動面板仍會安穩地繼續留在原處，像收起工具抽屜旁的小選單，桌上的工作紙不會一起被掃走。
body.en: The awkward moment when opening the “Switch Panel” menu made the whole panel disappear is gone. Previously, the temporary popover was already finished once the menu took focus, but its cleanup treated the floating panel as something to dismiss too. So pressing Escape, clicking the panel, or clicking elsewhere hid both the menu and the panel. Now cleanup closes only the menu. The floating panel stays, like folding away the little menu beside a tool drawer without sweeping the papers off your desk.

A transient popover was already gone by the time the menu took focus, so closing it was merely cleanup; the floating panel survives the menu, which turned the same cleanup into a mistouch that threw the panel away.

entries: **The Windows panel no longer snaps back to the primary monitor on every panel switch**: dragging the popover onto a second display and then switching panel style (or theme) forced it right back onto the primary monitor. Windows' `SPI_GETWORKAREA` API only ever reports the *primary* monitor's work area, and the window was clamped against that single rectangle on every reposition regardless of which monitor it actually lived on — so a window dragged onto a secondary display got clamped straight back onto the primary one the next time the panel reloaded. Placement now looks up the work area of whichever monitor the window's current (or saved) position falls on via `MonitorFromPoint`/`GetMonitorInfoW`, so a window on a secondary display stays there across panel switches. A related issue on a single monitor is fixed alongside it: switching panels reset the remembered content height to `None`, so the window was briefly clamped against each panel's near-fullscreen placeholder height (`PANEL_HEIGHTS`) before its real height was measured, which could shove a dragged window toward the top of the screen; the previous panel's measured height is now kept as the transitional estimate instead.

title.zh-TW: 切換面板不再把視窗送回主螢幕
title.en: Panel switching keeps your window on its monitor

body.zh-TW: 你把 Usage 的面板（跳出的浮動小視窗）拖到第二台螢幕，換個面板樣式或主題後，它終於不會又跳回主螢幕。以前 Windows 只把主螢幕可用範圍交給程式，程式每次重新定位面板時便拿錯尺，硬把第二台螢幕上的視窗推回去；現在會依面板目前或記住的位置，找出它所在螢幕的可用範圍再定位，所以換樣式後仍留在原處。單螢幕也一併修好：面板切換時會暫留前一種樣式量到的高度，等真正高度測完，不再先用接近全螢幕的假高度把你拖好的位置往上擠。像搬家工人終於先看你住哪一棟，再把家具放回那一棟，而不是一律送回一樓。
body.en: After you drag Usage's panel (a small floating pop-up) to a second monitor, switching its style or theme will finally leave it there. Windows had only handed the app the primary display's usable area, so each reposition used the wrong ruler and shoved the panel back onto the primary monitor. It now identifies the usable area for the display containing the panel's current or remembered position. On a single monitor, it also retains the previous style's measured height while the new one is measured, instead of briefly using a near-fullscreen placeholder that pushes your window upward. Like movers checking which building you live in before returning furniture, rather than always dumping it in the lobby.

Windows' `SPI_GETWORKAREA` API only ever reports the *primary* monitor's work area, and the window was clamped against that single rectangle on every reposition regardless of which monitor it actually lived on — so a window dragged onto a secondary display got clamped straight back onto the primary one the next time the panel reloaded. Placement now looks up the work area of whichever monitor the window's current (or saved) position falls on via `MonitorFromPoint`/`GetMonitorInfoW`, so a window on a secondary display stays there across panel switches. A related issue on a single monitor is fixed alongside it: switching panels reset the remembered content height to `None`, so the window was briefly clamped against each panel's near-fullscreen placeholder height (`PANEL_HEIGHTS`) before its real height was measured, which could shove a dragged window toward the top of the screen; the previous panel's measured height is now kept as the transitional estimate instead.

entries: **The panel no longer leaves an empty strip at the bottom**: panel height came from a fixed per-panel constant, so any layout that rendered shorter than the registered value left dead space below the footer. The common trigger is Codex reporting only a weekly window with no 5-hour data, which drops a quota row from the card. The panel now measures its own natural height after each refresh and the window resizes to match, clamped to the usable screen area; the registered constants stay as the pre-measurement default and as the fallback when a measurement is unusable. A panel that deliberately leaves room for a full-window backdrop — World Cup's pitch is the only one — marks that region so it keeps its designed height instead of collapsing while the measurement releases the layout's height constraints.

title.zh-TW: 額度面板會自己收好高度，不留底部空白
title.en: Quota panels now fit their content instead of leaving a blank strip

body.zh-TW: 你打開 Usage 面板（跳出來顯示額度的小視窗）查看 Codex 的每週額度時，底部不會再莫名多出一條空白帶。以前畫面高度照每張面板預設的固定值算；若 Codex 只回報每週時段、沒有 5 小時資料，額度卡少了一列，底下就留下死白。現在每次更新後，面板會量自己的實際高度，視窗隨著內容縮放，且不會超出可用螢幕範圍；量不出來時仍用原本數值當備援。這像量身裁衣：少一行內容就收短一點。只有 World Cup 的球場主題刻意預留滿版背景，會標記那塊空間，保留原本設計高度。
body.en: When you open the Usage panel to check Codex's weekly quota, an odd blank strip will no longer linger below it. The panel height used to come from a fixed preset. If Codex reported only a weekly window and no 5-hour data, the quota card lost one row but kept the extra height. Now, after each refresh, the panel measures its natural height and the window follows it without exceeding usable screen space; the old value remains a fallback if measuring fails. Think of a tailored hem: one less line of content, one less line of fabric. The World Cup pitch theme is the exception: it marks its intentional full-window backdrop so its designed height remains intact.

The common trigger is Codex reporting only a weekly window with no 5-hour data, which drops a quota row from the card. The panel now measures its own natural height after each refresh and the window resizes to match, clamped to the usable screen area; the registered constants stay as the pre-measurement default and as the fallback when a measurement is unusable. A panel that deliberately leaves room for a full-window backdrop — World Cup's pitch is the only one — marks that region so it keeps its designed height instead of collapsing while the measurement releases the layout's height constraints.

entries: **Claude Code panel no longer stays blank forever on Windows**: the installer picked whichever `python`/`py` `shutil.which()` found on `PATH` without checking it actually ran, so on any Windows machine without a real Python install, it silently wired the statusLine hook to Windows' non-functional "App Execution Alias" stub (the placeholder `python.exe`/`python3.exe` that Windows 10/11 ships by default to prompt a Microsoft Store install). The hook then failed silently on every refresh, `usage-status.json` was never written, and the Claude Code panel showed `--` permanently — not a first-run loading state. The installer now actually runs each candidate with `--version` before trusting it, and skips any that don't execute.

title.zh-TW: Windows 狀態列不再永遠空白
title.en: Windows status line no longer stays blank forever

body.zh-TW: Windows 電腦沒裝 Python 時，Claude Code 面板不會再永遠只顯示「--」。安裝程式原本只看 PATH（告訴電腦去哪找程式的搜尋名單）裡有沒有 `python` 或 `py`，卻沒確認它能不能跑；Windows 10、11 內建的 App Execution Alias 只是引你去 Microsoft Store 安裝的假 `python.exe`，也會被誤認。於是 statusLine hook（顯示在終端機最底下狀態列的掛鉤小程式）每次更新都靜悄悄失敗，`usage-status.json` 沒寫出來，面板便一直空白。現在安裝程式會先用 `--version` 實測候選程式，不能執行就跳過。像插座看似有孔、裡頭卻沒接電；現在會先試亮測電筆，才把線接上。
body.en: On a Windows PC without Python, the Claude Code panel will no longer show `--` forever. The installer used to trust any `python` or `py` found on PATH (the list of places Windows searches for programs) without checking whether it could run. Windows 10 and 11 ship an App Execution Alias: a placeholder `python.exe` that only sends you to Microsoft Store, yet it was mistaken for Python. The statusLine hook, a small program that updates the bottom status line, then failed silently on every refresh, so `usage-status.json` was never written. Now each candidate must pass `--version` first. It is like testing an outlet before plugging in the appliance.

items.original: **Claude Code panel no longer stays blank forever on Windows**: the installer picked whichever `python`/`py` `shutil.which()` found on `PATH` without checking it actually ran, so on any Windows machine without a real Python install, it silently wired the statusLine hook to Windows' non-functional "App Execution Alias" stub (the placeholder `python.exe`/`python3.exe` that Windows 10/11 ships by default to prompt a Microsoft Store install). The hook then failed silently on every refresh, `usage-status.json` was never written, and the Claude Code panel showed `--` permanently — not a first-run loading state. The installer now actually runs each candidate with `--version` before trusting it, and skips any that don't execute.

entries: **AI Council spends less Claude quota per turn**: `claude -p` calls without an attached project folder used to omit `--tools` entirely, so Claude Code loaded its full built-in toolset — Bash, Edit, Write, and the rest — into every turn's input even though the council prompt already tells participants not to call tools. Calls now pass `--tools ""` when no project folder is attached, and every Claude call adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to keep the system prompt prefix byte-stable across turns for a better shot at Anthropic's automatic prompt caching. Codex and Antigravity participants are unaffected.

title.zh-TW: AI Council 少帶一箱工具，Claude 額度更省
title.en: AI Council stops hauling unused tools into every Claude turn

body.zh-TW: AI Council 裡的 Claude 成員明明被要求只討論，卻每回合還背著一整箱用不到的工具，會白佔你的 Claude 額度。先前在沒有附上專案資料夾時，`claude -p` 沒有傳入 `--tools`，Claude Code 仍會把 Bash、Edit、Write 等內建工具（讓 AI 能執行終端機、編輯與寫入檔案的能力）整套塞進每回合的輸入。現在此情況會明確傳入 `--tools ""`，把工具箱留在門外。每次 Claude 呼叫也會加上 `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`，讓系統提示詞（AI 每回合先讀的固定規則）開頭在各回合維持位元組完全一致，較有機會命中 Anthropic 的自動提示詞快取（把已處理內容暫存直接沿用），少花重複額度。這只影響 Claude；Codex 和 Antigravity 成員不變。
body.en: In AI Council, Claude participants are told to discuss rather than use tools, yet they used to carry a whole unused toolbox into every turn, consuming Claude quota. When `claude -p` ran without an attached project folder, it omitted `--tools`, so Claude Code still packed its built-in tools—Bash, Edit, Write, and more—into each turn's input. It now explicitly sends `--tools ""` in that case, leaving the toolbox outside. Every Claude call also adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, keeping the system-prompt prefix byte-for-byte stable across turns and giving Anthropic's automatic prompt cache a better chance to reuse it. Codex and Antigravity participants are unchanged.

Calls now pass `--tools ""` when no project folder is attached, and every Claude call adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to keep the system prompt prefix byte-stable across turns for a better shot at Anthropic's automatic prompt caching. Codex and Antigravity participants are unaffected.

entries: **Steer the council mid-discussion**: an opt-in "guidance between rounds" toggle pauses the session before every round after the first, so you can react to what you just heard — "we're single-host, no cluster" — instead of watching a debate run off in the wrong direction or stopping and restarting from scratch. The pause waits up to 5 minutes and is skipped automatically if left blank; the round then proceeds exactly as it did before.

**See who disagreed, not just how many**: the consensus tally under the moderator's summary now lists each participant by name next to their stance, with dissenting and alternative positions colored so they stand out, instead of a bare "2 agree, 1 alternative" that meant scrolling back through the transcript to find out who.

**The five debate tones now explain themselves**: a one-line plain-language hint appears under the tone picker — devil's advocate, for instance, now reads "the AIs will deliberately argue the opposite side to test whether a plausible conclusion holds up" — so a first-time user isn't left guessing how "adversarial" differs from "devil's advocate."

title.zh-TW: AI 開會時能插話校正，也一眼看懂誰持反對意見
title.en: Steer an AI council as it talks, and see exactly who disagrees

body.zh-TW: 幾個 AI 正在替你討論方案，第一輪卻發現大家把你的單機需求當成要做叢集，也就是讓多台主機一起運作；現在不用整場喊停重來。開啟「輪次間指引」開關後，討論工作階段（一次連續進行的討論）每一輪結束、下一輪開始前都會暫停，讓你補一句「只有單一主機，不要叢集」。若一直空白，最多等五分鐘便自動略過，討論照原本方式繼續，像主持會議時每回合按一下暫停鈴，及早把話題拉回來。主持人摘要下方的共識統計（列出每位參與者採取的立場）也會直接寫出名字；反對與替代意見用顏色標出，不必再翻紀錄猜是誰說的。第一次挑辯論語氣時，五種選項下方都有白話提示；例如「魔鬼代言人」會刻意站到相反邊，測試看似合理的結論是否站得住腳，因此不會再把它和「對抗式」混為一談。
body.en: Picture an AI council discussing a plan, then learning after round one that your single-host setup is being mistaken for a cluster. You no longer need to scrap the whole discussion. Turn on “guidance between rounds” and the session pauses before every later round, so you can add a correction such as “single host, no cluster.” A blank pause skips itself after five minutes, then the next round continues normally—like a chairperson’s bell that gets the meeting back on topic early. The consensus tally beneath the moderator’s summary now names each participant beside their position and colors dissenting or alternative views, so you need not hunt through the transcript. New to the five debate tones? Each picker option now has a plain-language hint: devil’s advocate deliberately argues the other side to test whether a plausible conclusion actually holds up, rather than merely being adversarial.

items.original:
**Steer the council mid-discussion**: an opt-in "guidance between rounds" toggle pauses the session before every round after the first, so you can react to what you just heard — "we're single-host, no cluster" — instead of watching a debate run off in the wrong direction or stopping and restarting from scratch. The pause waits up to 5 minutes and is skipped automatically if left blank; the round then proceeds exactly as it did before.
**See who disagreed, not just how many**: the consensus tally under the moderator's summary now lists each participant by name next to their stance, with dissenting and alternative positions colored so they stand out, instead of a bare "2 agree, 1 alternative" that meant scrolling back through the transcript to find out who.
**The five debate tones now explain themselves**: a one-line plain-language hint appears under the tone picker — devil's advocate, for instance, now reads "the AIs will deliberately argue the opposite side to test whether a plausible conclusion holds up" — so a first-time user isn't left guessing how "adversarial" differs from "devil's advocate."

entries: **The menu bar critters no longer cost a third of a CPU core**: the phoenix, dragon and lion each drove their own timer, and every single frame re-sent the whole status item title to AppKit — which re-typesets the entire string through CoreText and re-measures the item's width, asking the system for its preferred languages along the way. With all three animating at full speed that came to 60 full relayouts a second, measured at 30–33% of a core with the popover closed; the cost arrived precisely when you were busiest, since the critters only animate while you are burning tokens. They now share a single timer, the fastest frame interval widens from 0.05s to 0.10s (indistinguishable on an 18px sprite), and a tick where no critter advances skips the redraw entirely. The burn-rate lookup that used to sit on the animation path — stat-ing 2,858 history files on the main thread every time its 30-second cache expired — moved to the background refresh, and the menu bar's text and sprite fragments are now cached instead of rebuilt per frame. Same animation, measured 4.2–5.9%.

**A service alert the provider forgot to clear no longer sticks around**: a status page can leave a component marked as degraded long after the incident is over, and the panel had no way to tell that apart from a live problem. Two rules now retire such an alert, both limited to the mildest *degraded performance* level so a partial or major outage is never hidden. First, if every unresolved incident on the page has sat in *monitoring* — the provider's own word for "the fix is in, we are watching it" — for more than four hours, the alert is suppressed until something changes. Second, a status observed unchanged for more than 24 hours is treated as residue. The second rule times what usage itself has seen rather than trusting the page's own timestamps: on OpenAI's page all 25 components, the operational ones included, share one timestamp from over two weeks earlier, so that field records when a component was defined, not when its status last moved.

title.zh-TW: 選單列小動物不再偷吃你的 CPU
title.en: Menu bar critters stop hogging your CPU

body.zh-TW: 你正趕著用 AI，選單列裡的鳳凰、龍、獅子卻可能反而拖慢電腦。它們只在燃燒 token（AI 處理與計費的文字單位）時動，原本各自用計時器，每秒重排畫面 60 次；連沒有角色換格的時刻也重畫。現在三隻共用一個計時器，最快節奏從 0.05 秒改為 0.10 秒，18px 小圖看不出差別，沒換格就不重畫。原先每 30 秒在主執行緒（程式處理畫面的主要路線）逐一查 2,858 個歷史檔的燃燒速率，也挪到背景更新；選單列的文字與圖像改用快取（把查過或算過的結果暫存直接用）。像三個人各搶同一盞舞台燈，如今輪流走位，動畫照樣在；面板關閉時實測 CPU 從一個核心的 30–33% 降至 4.2–5.9%。
body.en: When you are busy using AI, the phoenix, dragon, and lion in the menu bar used to slow your Mac down at exactly the wrong moment. They animate only while you burn tokens, but each had its own timer and together forced 60 full redraws every second, even when no critter had moved. Now they share one timer, the quickest frame interval changes from 0.05 to 0.10 seconds with no visible difference in an 18px sprite, and unchanged frames skip redraws. The burn-rate lookup no longer checks 2,858 history files on the main thread every 30 seconds; it refreshes in the background, while text and sprites are cached. Like three performers fighting over one spotlight, they now take turns. The animation remains, while measured CPU use drops from 30–33% of one core to 4.2–5.9%.

They now share a single timer, the fastest frame interval widens from 0.05s to 0.10s (indistinguishable on an 18px sprite), and a tick where no critter advances skips the redraw entirely. The burn-rate lookup that used to sit on the animation path — stat-ing 2,858 history files on the main thread every time its 30-second cache expired — moved to the background refresh, and the menu bar's text and sprite fragments are now cached instead of rebuilt per frame. Same animation, measured 4.2–5.9%.

title.zh-TW: 過期的服務警示會自己退場
title.en: Stale service alerts now clear themselves

body.zh-TW: 服務明明已恢復，面板卻還掛著警示，現在不會一直嚇你。供應商的狀態頁（顯示服務是否正常的公告頁）有時忘了清掉「效能下降」；usage 新增兩條只針對這個最輕等級的收線規則，部分或重大中斷絕不會被藏起來。第一條是：頁面上所有未結案事件都進入 monitoring（供應商表示修好後持續觀察的階段）超過四小時，警示先隱藏，直到狀態改變。第二條是 usage 自己連續看到同一狀態超過 24 小時，也把它當遺留資訊。為什麼不直接信頁面時間？OpenAI 狀態頁的 25 個元件連正常項目也共用兩週前的時間，那可能只是元件建立時間。這像商店門口忘了收回的「暫時缺貨」牌；只有確定是輕微狀況又久未更新才收起，真停業仍會留下。
body.en: A service can be back to normal while its panel still shows a warning. Usage now clears that kind of leftover alert without hiding a real outage. A provider status page may forget to remove a mild degraded-performance notice, so two retirement rules apply only to that lowest severity; partial and major outages always remain visible. First, if every unresolved incident has been in monitoring — the provider saying the fix is in and it is watching — for over four hours, the alert hides until something changes. Second, if Usage itself sees an unchanged status for more than 24 hours, it treats it as residue. Why not trust the page timestamp? All 25 OpenAI components, including healthy ones, share a timestamp more than two weeks old. It may mark when a component was created, not when its status changed. Like a shop's forgotten “temporarily out of stock” sign, only an old minor notice comes down; a real closure stays posted.

Two rules now retire such an alert, both limited to the mildest *degraded performance* level so a partial or major outage is never hidden. First, if every unresolved incident on the page has sat in *monitoring* — the provider's own word for "the fix is in, we are watching it" — for more than four hours, the alert is suppressed until something changes. Second, a status observed unchanged for more than 24 hours is treated as residue. The second rule times what usage itself has seen rather than trusting the page's own timestamps: on OpenAI's page all 25 components, the operational ones included, share one timestamp from over two weeks earlier, so that field records when a component was defined, not when its status last moved.

entries: **The council consensus tally no longer drops opinions**: stance labels were only matched at the very start of a turn's first line, so a rebuttal that reached its label a few words in — or ended its first line with one — counted as unparsed and vanished from the count. The whole first line is now scanned, and a turn must name exactly one distinct label to be counted; a turn quoting several stays unparsed instead of having one guessed for it.

**Every selected participant shows its check mark**: the "✓" marking a participant as joining the discussion is drawn as a CSS `::after` overlay, which never renders on a replaced element. It therefore appeared only on the seat whose avatar falls back to an inline SVG (Antigravity) and stayed invisible on the seats drawn from an image icon (Claude, Codex), making a fully selected line-up look half-selected. All three now host the overlay on a wrapper element.

**The disabled *start discussion* button says why it is disabled**: a line under the button now names what is missing — no topic, no participant selected, or a discussion already running — instead of leaving a greyed-out button and no explanation. The reason is tied to the button with `aria-describedby` and lives in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users get it too, not only whoever hovers.

**The moderator star is tellable apart**: all three stars carried the same accessible name, so a screen reader could not say which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes its pressed state, and its tooltip reads *current moderator* or *set as moderator* to match.

**Agreeing in a council rebuttal requires reasons**: a participant opening with the agreement stance must state what it reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain, so consensus cannot be reached by rubber-stamping.
Bumped `setuptools` to 83.0.0.

title.zh-TW: 共識不再漏算意見，也不能只靠一句同意
title.en: Consensus now counts every opinion and demands real agreement

body.zh-TW: 一場討論要有共識，不能靠有人開頭寫了「同意」就算數。council 討論（讓多位參與者各自表態後彙整結論的流程）以前只在每回合第一行開頭找立場標籤；先寫幾個字才標、或把標籤放在行尾，意見就像投票箱旁漏掉的選票，沒有被計入。現在會掃完整第一行，但一回合必須明確只提一種不同立場才列入；同時引用幾種立場就維持未解析，不隨便猜。若有人以同意立場開場，還得交代看過什麼、為何同意、仍有哪些顧慮。得出的共識不再是蓋章，而是每張選票都可追查的會議紀錄。
body.en: Consensus cannot rest on someone merely opening with “agree.” In a council discussion, where several participants state positions before a conclusion is collected, stance labels used to be checked only at the beginning of each turn’s first line. A label appearing later, or at line end, could disappear like a ballot dropped beside the box. The whole first line is now scanned, but a turn counts only when it names exactly one distinct label; a turn quoting several remains unparsed rather than being guessed at. An agreement opening must also say what was reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain. The result is less a rubber stamp than meeting minutes with every ballot traceable.

items.original:
**The council consensus tally no longer drops opinions**: stance labels were only matched at the very start of a turn's first line, so a rebuttal that reached its label a few words in — or ended its first line with one — counted as unparsed and vanished from the count. The whole first line is now scanned, and a turn must name exactly one distinct label to be counted; a turn quoting several stays unparsed instead of having one guessed for it.
**Agreeing in a council rebuttal requires reasons**: a participant opening with the agreement stance must state what it reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain, so consensus cannot be reached by rubber-stamping.

title.zh-TW: 選人與開始討論，介面終於說清楚
title.en: Selecting participants and starting a discussion are finally clear

body.zh-TW: 你選 Claude、Codex 或 Antigravity 加進討論時，每個被選中的座位現在都會亮出 ✓。先前這個記號綁在頭像本身，只有使用內嵌圖示的 Antigravity 碰巧顯示得出來；Claude 和 Codex 使用圖片頭像，整排明明都選好了，畫面卻像只選一半。現在三者都把記號放在外層，選取狀態一致可見。開始討論按鈕若變灰，底下也會說明是沒填主題、沒選參與者，還是已有討論正在跑。理由會連到按鈕並放進狀態區，鍵盤與螢幕閱讀器使用者也收得到，不必靠滑鼠懸停猜答案。像活動報名櫃台，名牌終於都掛在到場者胸前，不能開場時也會直接告訴你缺哪一項。
body.en: When you add Claude, Codex, or Antigravity to a discussion, every selected seat now shows a ✓. The mark used to sit on the avatar itself: it happened to appear for Antigravity’s inline SVG icon, but stayed invisible for Claude and Codex image avatars, making a fully selected lineup look half-selected. All three now place the overlay on a wrapper, so selection is consistently visible. If Start discussion is greyed out, text underneath now says whether the topic is missing, nobody is selected, or a discussion is already running. That reason is connected to the button and placed in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users receive it too. It is like a registration desk where every attendee finally gets a visible badge, and a closed door explains exactly what is still missing.

It therefore appeared only on the seat whose avatar falls back to an inline SVG (Antigravity) and stayed invisible on the seats drawn from an image icon (Claude, Codex), making a fully selected line-up look half-selected. All three now host the overlay on a wrapper element.
**The disabled *start discussion* button says why it is disabled**: a line under the button now names what is missing — no topic, no participant selected, or a discussion already running — instead of leaving a greyed-out button and no explanation. The reason is tied to the button with `aria-describedby` and lives in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users get it too, not only whoever hovers.

title.zh-TW: 主持人星號不再讓輔助工具猜人
title.en: Moderator stars no longer make assistive tools guess

body.zh-TW: 輪到你挑主持人時，三顆星星過去都對螢幕閱讀器說同一句話，根本無法清楚分辨到底哪一席正在主持。現在每顆星會公開自己的按下狀態，滑鼠提示也分成「目前主持人」或「設為主持人」。這改動看似小，卻讓不用看畫面的人能跟看得見的人一樣確認會議誰在掌舵。像舞台後的控台，三個按鈕以前都只寫「燈」，如今一眼或一聽就知道哪盞已經亮、按哪顆會換人。
body.en: When it is time to choose a moderator, the three stars used to give a screen reader the same accessible name, leaving no way to tell which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes whether it is pressed, and its tooltip says either “current moderator” or “set as moderator.” The change is small but lets people who do not view the screen confirm who is steering the meeting just as everyone else can. It is like a stage control board whose three buttons once all said “light”; now you can see or hear which lamp is on and which button changes it.

items.original: **The moderator star is tellable apart**: all three stars carried the same accessible name, so a screen reader could not say which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes its pressed state, and its tooltip reads *current moderator* or *set as moderator* to match.

title.zh-TW: 打包工具 setuptools 升到 83.0.0

body.zh-TW: 這版也把 setuptools（Python 用來打包與安裝套件的工具）升到 83.0.0。原始紀錄未說明對畫面或功能的影響；原始紀錄只交代這項相依套件升級，沒有承諾特定功能改變。對從原始碼安裝、打包或維護 Usage 的人，它像廚房換了新的量杯：原始紀錄沒有說明成品會有什麼變化。若你只是開啟成品使用，知道這是維護性更新即可；若你處理建置環境中的相依版本，則以 83.0.0 為準。
body.en: This release also moves setuptools, a Python tool for packaging and installing software, to 83.0.0. The source note does not describe any effect on the interface or features. The source notes only this dependency upgrade and do not promise a specific feature change. For someone installing from source, packaging, or maintaining Usage, it is like replacing a kitchen measuring cup. The source note does not say what changes, if anything, in the finished app. If you only use the finished app, treat this as maintenance. If you manage build dependencies, use 83.0.0 as the stated version.

entries: **Council participants can wear a persona from the AI Talent Market**: every seat now has a role picker next to its model picker, listing the specialists from your installed talent packs (contract review, front-end, security audit, and the rest). The role's expertise is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI can sit in two seats wearing two different hats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker — collapsed it shows only the pack names, so a 50-role list no longer scrolls off the screen. Role text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime and is never bundled into usage itself.

**Five debate styles for a council**: pick the tone every participant takes from the second round on — constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. The stance label each participant must open with is preserved under every style.

**Council consensus is counted, and can end the discussion early**: the stance labels participants open their rebuttals with are now tallied and shown above the summary. Turn on *end on consensus* and a discussion stops as soon as every participant in a round agrees, instead of burning through the rounds you budgeted for. A round where anyone failed to finish never counts as consensus.

**The moderator no longer sees who said what**: the transcript handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor the answers its own CLI wrote. Participant names are restored before the summary reaches your screen and the exported Markdown, so you still read "Claude argued…" rather than "Participant A argued…". Participants' own words are passed through untouched — a discussion *about* Claude or Codex stays readable.

title.zh-TW: 替 Council 每個座位配一頂專業帽子
title.en: Give every Council seat its own expert hat

body.zh-TW: 同一場 Council（讓多個 AI 分座討論的功能）裡，現在能替每個座位挑不同專長。想請一位看合約、一位找網頁問題、另一位做安全檢查時，模型選擇器旁的角色選擇器會列出已安裝人才包裡的專家。角色（persona，先替 AI 戴上的專業帽子）會以提示詞前綴加入，所以同一個 CLI（從命令列啟動的工具）可在兩張椅子分別扮演兩種人。角色會按人才包分組並可收合，五十個選項也不會把畫面捲到找不到底。角色文字則在執行時向 talent-market CLI 取得，不會塞進 usage 本身；像替一場會議現場選角，每張椅子都能坐上合適的專家。
body.en: In one Council (a feature where several AIs discuss an issue from separate seats), each seat can now take a different specialty. Need one person to review a contract, one to spot front-end trouble, and another to audit security? A role picker beside the model picker lists specialists from your installed talent packs. A persona (an expert hat placed on an AI before it speaks) is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI (a tool launched from a command line) can wear two different hats in two seats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker, keeping even 50 choices manageable. Their text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime instead of bundled into usage: like casting a meeting, each chair gets the right specialist.

The role's expertise is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI can sit in two seats wearing two different hats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker — collapsed it shows only the pack names, so a 50-role list no longer scrolls off the screen. Role text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime and is never bundled into usage itself.

title.zh-TW: 先決定辯論打法，同意就提早收場
title.en: Choose a debate style, then stop once everyone agrees

body.zh-TW: 一群 AI 反覆討論時，你可以先決定這場會議要當腦力激盪，還是挑錯大會。Council 從第二輪起可替每位參與者從五種辯論風格中選一種：找共識、挑漏洞、補缺口、蘇格拉底式追問假設，或唱反調的魔鬼代言人。無論選哪種，每人回應開頭的立場標籤都會保留，並統計在摘要上方。若打開 end on consensus（全員同意便停止的開關），某一輪人人標示同意時，討論會立刻結束，不會耗完原先預留輪數；只要有人沒完成該輪，便不算共識。像會議主席先訂好規則、再看全體舉牌，牌沒全舉起就不宣布散會。
body.en: When a group of AIs keeps debating, you can now decide whether the meeting should brainstorm together or hunt for flaws. From round two onward, Council lets each participant take one of five debate styles: constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. Whatever style you choose, the stance label opening each reply stays visible and is counted above the summary. Enable end on consensus (a switch that stops once everyone agrees), and the discussion ends as soon as every participant marks agreement in a round instead of using all budgeted rounds. If anyone fails to finish that round, it does not count. Like a chair setting meeting rules, then checking every raised hand before calling the room settled.

items.original:
**Five debate styles for a council**: pick the tone every participant takes from the second round on — constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. The stance label each participant must open with is preserved under every style.
**Council consensus is counted, and can end the discussion early**: the stance labels participants open their rebuttals with are now tallied and shown above the summary. Turn on *end on consensus* and a discussion stops as soon as every participant in a round agrees, instead of burning through the rounds you budgeted for. A round where anyone failed to finish never counts as consensus.

title.zh-TW: 主持人看不到名字，結論更不偏袒
title.en: Moderators no longer see names, keeping summaries impartial

body.zh-TW: 要主持人替多個 AI 的意見下結論時，現在它先看不到發言者姓名。交給主持人的逐字稿（transcript，完整保留每句話的討論記錄）已匿名化，避免它偏愛自己那個 CLI（從命令列啟動的工具）寫出的答案。摘要送回你的畫面或匯出成 Markdown（能直接排版的純文字格式）前，名字會恢復，所以你仍會讀到「Claude 主張……」，而非「參與者 A」。只有說話者的標記被遮住，原話不會改動；即使討論題目正是 Claude 或 Codex，內容也照樣看得懂。這像盲飲評酒：評審先喝內容、不看酒標，公布結果時才告訴你是哪一瓶。
body.en: When a moderator is asked to draw a conclusion from several AIs, it now sees the opinions before it sees their authors. The transcript (a record preserving every spoken line) handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor answers written by its own CLI (a tool launched from a command line). Names return before the summary reaches your screen or is exported as Markdown (plain text that can carry formatting), so you still read “Claude argued...” rather than “Participant A.” Only author labels are hidden; the words themselves remain untouched, even when the discussion is about Claude or Codex. It is like a blind wine tasting: judges taste what is in the glass before learning its label.

items.original: **The moderator no longer sees who said what**: the transcript handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor the answers its own CLI wrote. Participant names are restored before the summary reaches your screen and the exported Markdown, so you still read "Claude argued…" rather than "Participant A argued…". Participants' own words are passed through untouched — a discussion *about* Claude or Codex stays readable.
